title: Rung 1: recipe search and the compute-performance curve
design_ref: Predict before you spend: compute-performance curves
purpose: Run three recipes of the same small model for the same number of steps, measure held-out accuracy against compute, fit the design's saturating curve to each, and check what the fit can and cannot say.

steps.display: kubectl -n rl-scale get lws rollout   # 2 engine(s), settings: defaults
kubectl apply -f trainer-r1-center.yaml   # a JobSet: center (lr 3e-6)
steps.output:
CKPT_EVERY=1000
EVAL_EVERY=10
EVAL_PROBLEMS=200
GPUS_HELD=3
LEARNING_RATE=3e-6
MAX_CONCURRENT=64
MAX_STEPS=80

steps.display: kubectl apply -f trainer-r1-surrogate.yaml   # a JobSet: surrogate (no score centering)
steps.output:
CKPT_EVERY=1000
EVAL_EVERY=10
EVAL_PROBLEMS=200
GPUS_HELD=3
LEARNING_RATE=3e-6
MAX_CONCURRENT=64
MAX_STEPS=80
SCORE_CENTERING=0

steps.display: kubectl apply -f trainer-r1-lr1e6.yaml   # a JobSet: small step (lr 1e-6)
steps.output:
CKPT_EVERY=1000
EVAL_EVERY=10
EVAL_PROBLEMS=200
GPUS_HELD=3
LEARNING_RATE=1e-6
MAX_CONCURRENT=64
MAX_STEPS=80

steps.display: python fit_curves.py   # held-out pass rate against GPU hours, fitted with R0 + (A - R0) / (1 + (C_mid / C) ** B)
steps.output:
recipe                            start  end   ceiling A      B     C_mid(GPU h)
center (lr 3e-6)                  0.627  0.704  0.734 ± 0.444  6.00  0.241
surrogate (no score centering)    0.581  0.681  0.681 ± 0.034  1.41  0.081
small step (lr 1e-6)              0.598  0.649  1.000 ± 13.600  1.41  1.294

steps.display: python rank.py   # rank by ceiling only where the 2-standard-error intervals do not overlap
steps.output:
small step (lr 1e-6)  vs  center (lr 3e-6): not ranked: the intervals overlap
center (lr 3e-6)  vs  surrogate (no score centering): not ranked: the intervals overlap

steps.display: python rank.py --self-check   # the rule on three made-up ceilings: 0.70 and 0.69 (overlap), 0.55 (clear)
steps.output:
x vs y: not ranked: the intervals overlap
y vs z: ranked

steps.display: python extrapolate.py   # fit on the first half of each run, compare with the second half
steps.output:
center (lr 3e-6)                  mean |predicted - observed| = 0.051
surrogate (no score centering)    mean |predicted - observed| = 0.018
small step (lr 1e-6)              mean |predicted - observed| = 0.012

checks.description: each recipe ran 80 steps and was evaluated on the same 200 held-out problems at nine fixed steps
checks.because: The evaluation calls the rollout fleet's own API, so it measures the policy the fleet is serving, on the first 200 problems of the GSM8K test split, four samples each. The compute axis counts all three GPUs the run holds and leaves the evaluation's own time out.

checks.description: the starting score is the same for every recipe, within the evaluation's own noise
checks.because: All three start from the same model. A spread larger than the sampling noise of 800 samples (about 0.02 standard error) would mean the runs did not start from the same policy.

checks.description: the saturating curve fits every recipe and reports an uncertainty on the ceiling
checks.because: The ceiling A is the score the recipe approaches with unlimited compute; its standard error comes from the fit's covariance. A ceiling estimated from points that have not passed the curve's midpoint is weak, and the error shows it.

checks.description: the ranking rule refuses to rank recipes whose ceiling intervals overlap and ranks those that do not
checks.because: A ranking from overlapping intervals would be a coin flip dressed as a decision. The platform shows the interval and withholds the order.

checks.description: the fit on the first half of each run predicts the second half to within about three standard errors of the evaluation
checks.because: This is the trust the design says to attach to a curve: the gap between what the early part of the run predicted and what the later part showed. One evaluation of 800 samples has a standard error of about 0.02.
